However, on a very clear day with no dust or pollution, the sky can indeed appear blue. This is because the shorter, blue wavelengths of light are scattered more by the tiny molecules of gases in the atmosphere, a phenomenon known as Rayleigh scattering. This scattering effect makes the blue light more visible to our eyes, giving the sky its characteristic blue color.
